(8) explain the usage of adjectives, participles, infinitives, prefix and suffix conjugations, waw consecutive conjugation as well as concepts of perfective and non-perfective
(9) deduce the functions of each component after parsing a given sentence
(10) identify basic grammar implications in simple Hebrew sentences or phrases

Attitude Outcomes
(1) develop an interest and respect for the historical and cultural development of the Hebrew language from its paleo-Hebrew script until its Aramaic script, and the modern Hebrew language
(2) appreciate the distinctiveness of the Biblical Hebrew language
(3) cultivate an interest to read Biblical Hebrew texts

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Biblical Hebrew II
courses.description: This course, a sequel to Biblical Hebrew I, will continue to follow the textbook, Learn Biblical Hebrew by John H. Dobson (2005), covering Lessons 12–25. It will cover all the binyanim of Hebrew as well as understanding concepts of Hebrew syntax, function of prepositions and the principles of translating narratives and poetry and attempt a few exercises. In particular, we shall read the Masoretic text of the book of Jonah (a narrative with a poem) with the help of the Lexicons/Dictionaries and other Bible aids.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For students in Master of Divinity and MA in Theological Studies
Pre-requisite: Hebrew I (THEO1213 or THEO3217 or THEO5301)
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes

The students will be competent in the following abilities:

(a) recognize every component in the parts of speech learned in THEO5301

(b) identify the binyanim and functions of all verbs

(c) recall the forms and functions of the prepositions and particles

(d) identify, recognize at least 500 of the most common Biblical Hebrew words found in the Hebrew Bible

(e) search words in the Biblical Hebrew dictionaries and lexicons and explain the entries, in particular the BDB Lexicon.

(f) parse and translate given phrases/sentences and the book of Jonah

(g) use the parsing tools of Bible Works 10

(h) read and translate short narrative passages and some poems from the Hebrew Bible

(i) read and explain the grammar in the book of Jonah

Attitude Outcomes

The students will:

(a) be confident to read a Biblical Hebrew passage on their own with the necessary tools

(b) develop the habit of reading Biblical Hebrew passages

(c) appreciate the basic tasks to do exegesis and interpretation

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: New Testament Greek I
courses.description: This course provides students with an introduction to the basic grammar and vocabulary of New Testament Greek, in order to enable students to read the original New Testament texts.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity and MA in Theological Studies
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
On the successful completion of this unit, students should be able to:
1. master the basic syntax and a working vocabulary of New Testament Greek; and
2. read and translate simple Greek texts

Attitude Outcomes:
Throughout the learning process, students are expected to:
1. develop a regular revision practice;
2. develop a positive attitude to face difficulties in learning; and
3. develop an initiative to help others and seek help from others by means of group study.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: New Testament Greek II
courses.description: This course is a continuation of New Testament Greek I. It provides students with an introduction to the essential elements to New Testament Greek. Students will master different aspects of Greek morphology and syntax and acquire a substantial reading vocabulary. In order to enhance learning, the course employs both deductive and inductive methods.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For students in Master of Divinity and MA in Theological Studies
Pre-requisite(s): New Testament Greek I (THEO1215 or THEO3215 or THEO5303)
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
On the successful completion of this unit, students should be able to:
1. master the essential Greek morphology and syntax and a handful vocabulary of New Testament Greek; and
2. read and translate complex Greek sentences with the aid of lexicons.

Attitude Outcomes:
Throughout the learning process, students are expected to:
1. develop a regular revision practice;
2. develop a positive attitude to face difficulties in learning; and
3. develop an initiative to help others and seek help from others by means of group study.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
courses.description: This course orientates students to the diverse scholarship which encompasses the study of the Hebrew Scripture: from archaeology, historical-critical, grammatico-historical, socio-historical methodologies to the history of composition of the biblical books, languages, religions and literature of the period before the common era. Inevitably, it also introduces the world of the ancient Near East – its history, religions and literature, which the Hebrew Scripture belonged and related to. This course traces the challenges confronted bythe nation of Israel from its beginning up until the period of the Second Temple.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For students in Master of Divinity
Exclusion: THEO5919 The Hebrew Bible in Contexts
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
1. The students will know and understand
a. the general overview of the contents in the Hebrew Bible
b. the direct relationship of the composition of the books to her contexts
c. a general grasp of the scholarship pertaining to the study of the Hebrew Bible
2. The students can describe, explain and discuss
a. the main issues related to the composition and redaction of the books in the Hebrew Bible
b. the main issues of critical scholarship concerning the origin and identity of Israel
c. the proposed historical contexts of the Hebrew Bible
d. the relationships or/and tensions between the traditions underlying the theological motivations and the contemporary
e. situation/s of the text

Attitude Outcomes:
The students will appreciate
a. the making/compilation of the Hebrew Bible
b. the necessity for language acquisition in the study of the Hebrew Bible
c. the diverse research faculties in the study of the Hebrew Bible

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Introduction to the New Testament
courses.description: The main purpose of this course is to give students a general understanding the text of the New Testament, its methods of studies, its background and the issues involved. To achieve this purpose, it is necessary for students to know how the NT is interpreted in the light of modern thoughts. This involves firstly a good knowledge of the meaning of the basic text of the NT - this is in fact the prerequisite condition for students who are going to take this course; those do not know the text of the NT have to read through it twice (both students who are going to take this course; those do not know the text of the NT have to read through it twice (both Chinese and English version) at least. Besides, students are also required to read some basic works of modern interpretation of the NT.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For students in Master of Divinity
Exclusion THEO5910 New Testament in Contexts
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
1. To give students a general understanding the text of the New Testament, its methods of studies, its background and the issues involved; and
2. To be able to grasp the method of Bible study and exegesis, particularly Pauline Letters.
Skills Outcomes:
1. To enhance critical intelligence thinking; and
2. To enhance analytical ability throughout exegesis.
Attitude Outcomes
1. To develop one’s ability to have a critical and yet sympathetic understanding and appreciation of different church traditions and scholarly perspectives; and
2. To develop one’s sensitivity to the limit of doctrines and enhance openness to different exegesis.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Wisdom and the Psalms
courses.description: This course studies the “wisdom” genre of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament, namely Job, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Ecclesiasticus and the Wisdom of Solomon, and some wisdom passages in the prophetic genre, as well as the book of Psalms. It studies the concept of “wisdom” in these books, and their distinction from, and relation to the other books of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament. At the same time, it also considers its relationship to the ancient Near East genre of instruction literature.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
1. The students will know and understand
a. the historical background to the wisdom literature as genre in the Old Testament and the general scholarship
b. the rudimentary of Hebrew poetry
c. the general scholarship pertaining to scholarship in Psalms
2. The students can describe, explain and evaluate
a. the major literary features of wisdom books and the division in the Books of Psalms
b. the major themes, purposes and historical contexts and relevance of the individual books
c. the relationship between Psalms, the wisdom literature and the other genres and books of the Old Testament
d. the relevance of these books to the world today

Attitude Outcomes:
The students will appreciate:
a. the relevance of this genre to other cultures and their distinctions
b. the emotional and spiritual livelihood of Israel in relation to their deity as they confront political and societal challenges

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Synoptic Gospels
courses.description: This course comprises a study of the purpose and theology of the Synoptic Gospels (Matthew, Mark and Luke), comparing their distinct characteristics and looking at their similarities and differences. The course begins with a critical survey of the history of the Synoptic problem (how to explain the relationship between Matthew, Mark, and Luke) and proposed solutions. Exegesis of selected passages will be carried out to understand the original setting of individual gospel.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
1. To have basic knowledge of the content of the Synoptic Gospels;
2. To be sensitive to the similarities and differences of the Synoptic Gospels; and
3. To be able to grasp the method of Bible study and exegesis, particularly Synoptic Gospels.
Skills Outcomes:
1. To enhance critical intelligence thinking; and
2. To enhance analytical ability throughout exegesis.
Attitude Outcomes:
1. To develop one’s ability to have a critical and yet sympathetic understanding and appreciation of different church traditions and scholarly perspective; and
2. To develop one’s sensitivity to the limit of doctrines and enhance openness to different exegesis.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Johannine Literature
courses.description: This course will include a study of the authorship, purpose and main themes of the Johannine literature. Special attention will be given to some selected passages from the Gospel according to John, the Epistles of John and Revelation (Apocalypse).
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
1. To have basic knowledge of the content, theology and historical contexts of Johannine Literature (including Apocalypse);
2. To have basic knowledge of the so-called "Johannine Community";
3. To be able to understand particularly the Gospel of John (or the Apocalypse); and
4. To be able to grasp the method of Bible study and exegesis, particularly Johannine Literature.

Skills Outcomes:
1. To enhance critical intelligence thinking; and
2. To enhance analytical ability throughout exegesis.

Attitude Outcomes:
1. To develop one’s ability to have a critical and yet sympathetic understanding and appreciation of different church traditions and

2. To develop one’s sensitivity to the limit of doctrines and enhance openness to different exegesis.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Pauline Letters
courses.description: This course is a study of the Pauline and Deuteropauline Letters. Through comparing some of the critical passages from both categories, the course will explore the dating, authorship, purpose and the development of the Pauline theology.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
1. To have basic knowledge of the content, theology and historical context of Pauline Letters;
2. To have basic knowledge of historical Paul;
3. To be able to understand particularly the first letter of Pauline Letters (i.e. the Letter to the Romans); and
4. To be able to grasp the method of Bible study and exegesis, particularly Pauline Letters.

Skills Outcomes:
1. To enhance critical intelligence thinking; and
2. To enhance analytical ability throughout exegesis.

Attitude Outcomes:
1. To develop one’s ability to have a critical and yet sympathetic understanding and appreciation of different church traditions and scholarly perspectives; and
2. To develop one’s sensitivity to the limit of doctrines and enhance openness to different exegesis.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Pentateuchal Studies
courses.description: This course covers the major scholarship pertaining to the books of Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. It not only examines the themes and historical purposes for these books, but also orientates the students to the complexities of the contents and purposes for these books as evidenced by the prominent scholarship throughout the 19th to the 21st century. It tracks the recent development of the debates pertaining to the source theories of J, E, D and P; and also recent alternative theories and methodologies to the study of the Pentateuch.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
The students will know and understand:
a. the general influence of the ancient Near East cultures on the composition of the Pentateuch
b. the scholarship on Pentateuch in relation to the composition, history, themes and methodologies of interpretations from 19th – 21st century
c. the source theories of J, E, D and P.
The students can describe, explain and discuss and evaluate
a. the themes and purposes of the Pentateuch
b. the historical and social contexts of the Pentateuch
c. the relationship of the Pentateuch to the rest of the Hebrew Bible
d. the contemporary scholarship emerging in Pentateuchal scholarship with regards to methodologies of interpretation
e. the current status of J, E, D and P.

Attitude Outcomes:
The students will appreciate:
a. the process of the composition, redaction and transmission of the Pentateuch
b. the significance of Pentateuch to the Jews and its continual influence on the three communities of faith: Judaism, Islam and Christianity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Prophetic Literature
courses.description: This course covers selected readings from the second portion of the Hebrew bible, the Prophets, in particular the latter prophets, which includes Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and the book of the Twelve (Minor Prophets). Historical studies aided with contextual interpretations will be the approach taken in engaging the biblical text, while theological and exegetical studies of the text will interact vigorously with contemporary social, political, economic and cultural dimensions of the public life. Insights and influences from modern literary and critical theories, social sciences and humanities, and various inter-disciplinary approaches will also be introduced and applied in the course of interpretation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge Outcomes:
(1) To be able to understand prophetic literature in terms of its historical scholarship and contemporary interpretations.
(2) To be able to engage the prophetic text with contemporary contextual issues.
Attitude Outcomes
(1) To develop students’ ability to have a critical and yet sympathetic understanding and appreciation of the prophetic literature of
the Hebrew bible within the milieu of modern biblical scholarship.
(2) To develop students’ sensitivity to the relevancy of biblical prophetic literature to the public dimension of human life.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: The book of Ezra-Nehemiah and the books of Chronicles
courses.description: This course focuses on the books of Ezra, Nehemiah and Chronicles in the Hebrew Bible, which are important parts of Hebrew Bible Historiography reflecting the situation of the Jews in the Second Temple Period. The scholarship associated with the Second Temple/Persian Period is also soaring in new and exciting frontier which we hope this course can help students to follow such a trend. Issues including textual criticism, authorship and readership, sources, theme and theology will be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Early and Medieval Church
courses.description: The purpose of the course is to introduce the students to the historical and theological developments in the early and medieval church, from Jesus to the dawn of the Reformation and to engage them in a critical dialogue with earlier forms of contextualization of the Christian faith.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
a) The students will gain a general knowledge of the theological and ecclesial development during the covered period.
b) The students become familiar with key doctrinal development and the interplay between religious institutions and socio-political circumstances of the early and medieval period of the church.
c) The students will get acquainted with different perspectives on church history and with issues that are still debated.
d) The students will develop sensitivity regarding the diversity of Christian faith expressions and gain historical depth in their theological reflection.
e) The students learn about historical forms of contextualization.
f) The critical study of church history helps the students to recover the voices of those who have been condemned as heresy.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: History of Christianity in Hong Kong
courses.description: This course aims at helping students to gain a comprehensive understanding on the history of Protestant Christianity in Hong Kong. The first section will emphasize on the historical development of Christianity in different stages. The second section will investigate the relationship and interaction between Christianity and Hong Kong society from topical perspectives.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Learning outcomes
(1) To assist students to understand the historical development of Christianity in Hong Kong.
(2) To assist students to acquaint the methods of conducting research on local church history
Attitude Outcomes
(1) To develop and affirm students’ identity towards local church history

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: History of Christianity in China
courses.description: This course aims at giving the students a macro historical picture of Christianity in China from the seventh century to the present. Special attention will be paid to the interaction between Christianity and the Chinese society.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Learning outcomes
(1) To assist students to understand the historical development of Christianity in China
(2) To assist students to acquaint the methods of conducting research on Chinese church history
Attitude Outcomes
(1) To develop and affirm students’ identity towards Chinese church history

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: History of Christianity in Asia
courses.description: The course introduces the students to the history of Christianity in Asia, from the first century and the mission to India through the Sassanid and the Mongolian period, the spread of Roman-Catholic and Protestant faith in the colonial era to the development of independent Christianity since the 20th century. A significant focus of the course will be on more recent developments in different parts of Asia.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
a) The students will gain an understanding of the historical development of Christianity in Asia and will learn to perceive and appreciate Christianity in Asia as a partly parallel and independent rather than as latter development to Christianity in Europe.
b) The students will learn about the contemporary challenges of Christian churches in different contexts of Asia and the reasons for different growth developments. They will learn to distinguish between joint Asian concerns and the concerns of particular contexts.
c) In the different historical developments of Christianity in Asia, the students will encounter different models of Christianity and Christian relations to their cultural environment. The students will equally discover different issues of contextualization.
d) The students will develop sensitivity regarding mission, ecumenism, and contextualization in the postcolonial Asian context and learn about different Christian responses to the multi-religious context of Asia. The focus on the diversity of Christian churches and faith expressions in Asia leads beyond the dualism of local church and church in the West and helps perceive Christianity in a multi-polar world.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Humanity and Salvation
courses.description: This course introduces both the historical and theological development of Christian doctrine of humanity and salvation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To acquire the basic knowledge of Christian doctrine of humanity and salvation.
2. To gain an integrated theological perspective and methodology so that students can be critically engaged in theological construction.
3. To have a positive commitment to human welfare.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Systematic Theology I
courses.description: Systematic theology can be understood as the theological discipline that constructively articulates the meaning, coherence, and implications of Christian beliefs. This course aims at providing students with a solid methodological foundation for the study of systematic theology by investigating various issues that belong to the “prolegomena” of systematic theology, including the formative factors of theology (such as revelation, Bible, tradition, experience, reason, and culture), theological language, and theological methods.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes: After completing this course, the student is expected (a) to have an historical overview of the major paradigms in Christian theology; (b) to understand significant issues and diverse views regarding the formative factors of theology (especially the Bible, but also tradition, culture, theological language, etc.); (c) to have basic knowledge of exemplary theological systems and methods; (d) to be able to think analytically and critically in the field of theology.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Systematic Theology II
courses.description: After completing this course, the student is expected (a) to a solid understanding of major Christian doctrines, including the diversity of views, major historical developments, and significant issues involved, and their interrelations; (b) to be able to read and understand the writings of some important theologians, especially those in the patristic era, the Reformation era, and the twentieth century; (c) to be able to critically articulate the relevance of systematic theology for Christian life and churches.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes: After completing this course, the student is expected (a) to a solid understanding of major Christian doctrines, including the diversity of views, major historical developments, and significant issues involved, and their interrelations; (b) to be able to read and understand the writings of some important theologians, especially those in the patristic era, the Reformation era, and the twentieth century; (c) to be able to critically articulate the relevance of systematic theology for Christian life and churches.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Local Church Study
courses.description: This course aims at helping students to gain a comprehensive understanding on the history of the field of study namely congregational study. It also helps student to critically understand the theologies behind different models of church, and how these theologies of church are translated into practice in the practical world. Special attention will be paid to the Hong Kong church--its historical developoment, its theologies, its denominational traditions, polity and others. Students will have chance to analyse their own churches according to what they learn from class.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
知識方面：
從歷史角度初步了解本地新教之發展與現況
把握本地新教堂會的社會學及神學實況
學習分析影響著本地新教堂會發展之幾個因素
認識堂會研究之方法及方法論基礎
態度方面：
對堂會發展與現況持批判而開放的態度
更關心本地堂會發展
技巧方面：
能初步以堂會研究之方法去分析本地教會議題

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Pastoral Theology
courses.description: This course covers three areas: 1) the historical and theological position of Pastoral Theology in Theological Studies and its uniqueness; 2) different types of Pastoral Theology and their aims; and 3) Ancient and contemporary church models and pastoral emphases.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
To understand what is Pastoral Theology with reflection from personal pastoral experience.
To construct Pastoral Theology from the Bible, church and Chinese cultural traditions.
To understand different emphases of Pastoral Theology from multiple perspectives and from histories of different denominations.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Denominational Tradition and Polity
courses.description: The course is aimed at deepening the students’ understanding of the historical background, the theological basis and the church practice of one of the denominational traditions of the supporting churches of Divinity School of Chung Chi College. The critical reflection of the denominational tradition and polity equips the students to identify patterns of transformation and change in a denominational tradition and guide them in devising strategies for the continuous reform of tradition and polity.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
a) Knowledge about the history of the church tradition
b) Understanding of theological orientation
c) Familiarity and understanding of the specific liturgical practice
d) Acquaintance with the social and educational service and the missionary outreach.
e) Understanding of congregational growth patterns and ability to apply analytical tools for the analysis of growth patterns.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Homiletics

meetings.instructor:
Dr. LI Kwan Hung Leo, 
Professor YIP Ching Wah Francis

courses.description:
This course will cover: 1) the principles, construction and technique in preaching; and
2) the content and message of a sermon in contemporary world. This course will include video-taping students’ preaching. Tutorials after preaching will be conducted for the improvement of technique and content.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
To understand the principle of preaching on theological topics.
To understand the integration of different types of preaching and the way of preparation.
To learn and practice the techniques and styles in delivering a sermon.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Liturgics
courses.description: The course aims at equipping students with the understanding of the history and theology of the sacred worship, which include the development of the sacred worship, the notion of liturgical time, of ecclesiastical year, of sacred space, of Monastic and Cathedral office, of the liturgy of the hours. It also helps student to gain a critical understanding on various liturgical terms, liturgical vessels, books and vestments. Contextualization of liturgy in Chinese/HK contexts will also be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. students will gain critical understanding on the history and theology of sacred worship.
2. students will be able to apply the knowledge gain from this course to their own ecclesiastical context.
3. students will acquire basic but core skills in appropriately performing liturgies.
4. students will be able to develop their own visions on how the liturgical traditions should be contextualized in the Chinese context

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Preaching
courses.description: Through lectures, reading and self-studies, students learn how to compose and deliver sermon. Special emphasis will be given to Biblical exposition, progression of thoughts, flow of feelings, use of illustrations, relevancy, and deliver styles. Critiques, suggestions, or comments by the instructor and interaction in a small group will be facilitated. Each student is expected to deliver a full-length sermon in front of other students two to three times a semester and hand in the relevant scripts at the same time. Students need to hand in the revised scripts in two weeks’ time.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes: Learn how to compose and deliver sermons of 30 minutes and learn how to make comments and give suggestions to sermons preached by others.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Death and Dying
courses.description: This course explores the meaning of death and its related issues from different perspectives, namely, religious, pastoral, philosophical and sociological in order that students can develop sensitivity and skill in meeting and serving the dying as well as the bereaved.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To understand different perspectives on death and dying.
2. To acquire students with knowledge and necessary skill how to take care of the dying and bereaved.
3. To reinforce values of empathy, hope, courage and solidarity.
4. To become more confidence in skill in academic context via writing and speaking.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Foundation of Religious Education
courses.description:
This course aims at providing opportunities for students:
1. To look at the foundational theories of Religious Education;2. To deepen their knowledge and understanding of such theories from the perspective of the Christian religion;3. To apply such theories in assessing exercises of assessing courses/programs of Christian Education currently used in denominations and local churches;4. To apply such theories by developing a model of Christian Education with a new approach entitled “Praxis in Dimensions”.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Approaches to Mission Studies
courses.description: The course introduces students to the broad subject of mission studies and the understanding of issues related to the mission of the church. In particular it will lead to a deeper understanding about the biblical basis of the mission of the church, about the historical development of Christian mission, about contemporary challenges that the mission of the churches faces, about patterns of mission today, about contextualization, more particularly about mission in the context of Hong Kong and China.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
• The students will develop an understanding of a variety of missionary patterns and paradigms.
• The students will be able to critically review different approaches in Christian mission and evangelism and make informed and appropriate judgment about their contextual character.
• The students will apply their diagnostic skills to evaluate specific mission agencies and organizations from within their ecclesial context.
• The students will learn to creatively design a mission outreach plan to specific people groups.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Christian Ethics
courses.description: This course examines the context, nature, method and principles of Christian ethics. Emphasis is given to contemporary challenges to and of Christian ethics.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To understand the diversities of Christian ethics and its challenges.
2. To acquire students with knowledge to critically reflect the contemporary issues.
3. To make appropriate critical connections between the study of Christian ethics, practical theology and biblical studies.
4. To appreciate the impact that one’s values and decisions make on the lives of oneself and others.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Students are provided an opportunity to conduct a research on a chosen topic within the area of study with the agreement of a faculty member.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Theological Studies
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will acquire the knowledge, skills, and attitude required to conduct in-depth research of his chosen topic.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Research Paper in Christian Studies
courses.description: To enhance independent research in Christian studies, the course is required to submit an extended research paper not less than 15,000 words on an approved topic written under the supervision of a member of the teaching staff.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Christian Studies;Prerequisite: THEO5906

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Preaching Bible in Contexts
courses.description: The course encourages and equips contextual interpretation and contextual proclamation of the Bible. "Contexts" are existential, life-oriented and multifaceted, e.g. political, economic, cultural, geographical, religious, personal growth, etc. "Context" could also be determined by liturgical demands such as Sunday sermon, baptism, Eucharist, festival, funeral, wedding ceremony and so forth. Students are expected to bridge the ancient biblical context(s) with the contemporary life context(s).
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Homiletics and Selected Reading of the Bible
courses.description: The course encourages dialogue between pastors and biblical scholar(s) concerning theory and praxis. Both parties are engaged to build up a constructive relationship between critical exegesis and ecclesiastical preaching. Sermon topic related to specific area of biblical studies (such as Wisdom Literature, Pauline Letters, the Apocalypse of John, etc.) will be selected. Instead of motivational speaking, students are expected to prepare and deliver sermons in light of scholarly consensus, updated biblical studies and accountable exposition of the Bible.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Teaching Bible in Church and School
courses.description: The course investigates the history, current situation and new trends of educational ministry within the Church and schools with church background (including local churches, denominations, kindergartens, primary schools and secondary schools). Implementation experiences of "Sunday" school, Bible study group and religious studies subjects at school are consolidated and evaluated. Strategies for better implementation of Bible teaching are formulated. Students are expected to manage and plan the Bible ministries in their church or school setting effectively.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: The Bible and Worship
courses.description: The course concerns itself with the liturgical study of selected psalms, the investigation of the Sitz im Leben of the church in worship; much attention will be given to the didactic materials bearing on corporate worship in the Bible and their application for today’s church.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge outcome: The student will study the Scriptures especially the psalms against the context in order to develop a biblical understanding of worship.

Attitude outcome: The student is asked to cultivate an openness and personal vulnerability to the biblical sources.

Skill outcome: The student is expected to think biblically in the planning and conduct of corporate worship.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Theology of Worship
courses.description: Worship is styled as theologia prima, and doctrine as theologia secunda；not a few hymnic and confessional materials are found in the New Testament. The course will discuss various theologies of worship, the pastoral therapeutic efficacy of the sacraments, the functions of signs and symbols bearing on worship.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Knowledge outcome: The student is asked to cultivate a more theological understanding of why we are doing what in the conduct of Christian worship.

Attitude outcome: The student is expected to nurture a sense of sacredness and respectfulness wherever he/she finds himself/ herself towards the people and the world.

Skill outcome: The study of theology of worship is not only academic, but for personal enrichment, spiritual growth.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Congregational Hymns and Pastoral Care
courses.description: The course concerns itself with the criteria and evaluation of congregational hymns and their liturgical function in corporate worship; the selection of congregational hymns for the church calendar and theme of worship; their dual function of expression and impression for pastoral care.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
The Student will be able to:

1. Be familiar with the function and role of hymns in the corporate worship and Christian life.

2. Select hymns with theological, liturgical, and pastoral discernment.

3. Deal with issues regarding congregational songs of the 21st century as a theologian and pastor.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Planning and Leading Worship Service
courses.description: This course explores the practical ways of planning and leading public worship service of our time applying the reflections of biblical and historical perspectives of worship. Special attention will be given to diverse expressions of worship elements, creative ways of leading corporate worship, and evaluation of current worship practices. Students collaborate to plan and lead worship service.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students are able to:

1. Articulate biblical and historical perspectives on worship.

2. Develop corporate worship services implementing diverse traditional creative expressions of worship elements relevant to a local church.

3. Lead worship services in an effective and confident way.

4. Demonstrate scholarly informed perspectives on issues associated with corporate worship of our time.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Church Organist Training
courses.description: The class discusses the skills and techniques of hymn playing and anthem accompanying on the organ. Students will learn how to combine organ repertoire into church liturgies, and also explore different styles of service playing from the Baroque period to the modern time. Students can take this course for up to 3 terms (total of 3 credits). Pianists are welcomed to register for the course but an audition will be required.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
The student is expected to develop a high proficiency in music making, and be able to lead a worship service through music. Throughout the term, the student will look into a special topic that is related to the history of organ/ service playing (e.g. registrations of Bach chorale preludes, French Organ Mass of the 17th Century, Tradition of Hymns and Anthems Playing in England in the 19th Century, etc)

The student should also be self-motivated and practise the assigned organ pieces diligently on a daily basis.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Preaching According to the Lectionary
courses.description: Preaching according to the lectionary is a time-honored tradition of the church. The four lessons of Old Testament, Psalm, Epistle and the Gospel for the Sunday are carefully arranged to be read and preached according to the liturgical year. The course concerns itself with the liturgical, spiritual import as well as the pastoral application of the lectionary for today’s church alongside the understanding of the basics and recent discussions of homiletics.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Learning outcome: Students learn to appreciate the spiritual, liturgical import as well as the inter-connection of the four lessons of the Psalm, Old Testament, Epistle and the Gospel.

Attitude outcome: Student should appreciate the ecumenical endeavor and collaboration in the production of the revised common lectionary and resourceful heritage of the faith community.

Skill outcome: Student is expected to dwell on the liturgical import of the lectionary in the preparation of the sermon.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Life Education in Hong Kong
courses.description: The course is to explore ideas, practices and pedagogies of life education in Hong Kong, and its relation to new issues emerging from value education, such as national identity and service learning. Apart from lectures, this course will arrange workshops, local and/or overseas field trips.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity and MA in Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes:
1 To acquire basic understanding of the ideas of life education

2 To learn the practices of life education through experiential learning and field study.

3 To reflect critically the pedagogies of life education

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Ethics, Society and Religion
courses.description: This course attempts to explore the complexity of contemporary issues raised by ethics and society through a religious perspective.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To adopt multi-disciplinary approaches to identify, analyze and evaluate the contemporary issues.
2. To articulate and apply religious resources to respond to the contemporary issues.
3. To develop appropriate manner, honest exchange of idea and skill to solve problems in group discussions.
4. To use public reasoning to communicate the findings to a range of audiences.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Religious Education and Personal Growth
courses.description: This course will attempt to study some of the modern developmental theories such as Piaget’s cognitive developmental theory, Erikson’s socio-psychological theory, Kohlberg’s moral developmental theory and Fowlers’ faith developmental theory. Special attention will be given to the evaluation of their signifi cance to education in a religious context.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completing the course, students should be able to:
a. comprehend the developmental themes throughout the life span and the related theories of developmental psychology.
b. understand the theories related to moral, faith and spiritual development.
c. self-examine the student’s own understanding and philosophy of religious education.
d. self-examine the student’s stage of personal and spiritual development, reflecting on the implications for her/his role as a religious educator.
e. critically apply concepts in developmental psychology to specific educational contexts.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Culture, Religion and Ethics
courses.description: This course attempts to articulate the creative inquiry into and conceptual interrelationship among culture, religion and ethics. Particular attention is given to the relevance of theological reflection for cultural analysis in public life, the advance of technology, the movement of economic order, the ambiguity of sexual issue and the pressing demands for dialogue between the world’s religions.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To adopt multi-disciplinary approaches to identify, analyze and evaluate the common concerns of culture, religion and ethics.

2. To develop appropriate manner, honest exchange of idea and skill to solve problems in group discussions.

3. To use public reasoning to communicate the findings to a range of audiences.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Religion and Ecological Crisis
courses.description:
This course aims at introducing the students to the issues related to religion and
environmental ethics. The course will cover the following aspects: the basic approaches in environmental ethics; how religions are related to the environmental problems; the worldview and ethics of the major religious traditions; and how contemporary religions respond to the environmental question.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To identify and review critically the relationship between ecology and religion.

2. To apply the knowledge and skill developed in the course creatively to design religious responses to environmental questions.

3. To develop appropriate manner, honest exchange of idea and skill to solve problems in group discussions.

4. To make formal presentation on the theme of religion and ecological crisis to the public.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: THEORIES OF RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
courses.description: This course examines various theories of religious education. It begins with an historical overview of different approaches to religious education. It then examines some influential theories of religious education, particularly James Fowler's comprehensive theory of faith development, Paulo Freire's praxis approach to education, and Thomas Groome's theory of Christian religious education. Students will explore contributions, as well as limitations, of these theories to religious education classroom of contemporary Hong Kong.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Christian Education in the Postmodern World
courses.description: This course explores the dynamics of living in a postmodern world and its impact on Christian education. It will first describe the emergence and meaning of postmodernity. It will then explore its impact on religion in general and Christian education in particular. Issues like religious convictions, moral decisions, and character and spiritual formation will be of particular interest. Lastly, students are expected to rediscover the meanings of Christian education in the postmodern world.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Teaching/Learning Theories in Christian Education
courses.description: This course explores theories of teaching and learning in an effort to enhance teaching effectiveness in the field of Christian Education. Attention will be given to the examination of historical and contemporary models of teaching/learning and, the development of personal pedagogies for Christian Education in schools and churches.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completing the course, students should be able to:
1. understanding the role of Christian Education in wider cultural, social, and educational contexts; and its cross-curricular significance in schools
2. develop creative and imaginative teaching and learning strategies in Christian Education through cross-curricular approaches
3. critically explore how Christian Education can inform school curriculum, organization, teaching, educational leadership, and student culture.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Christian Education and Character Formation
courses.description: This course is designed to equip educators with vision and accompanying skills for aligning Christian education to character formation. Students will be guided in developing a general understanding of how character is formed in childhood and throughout the lifespan. Different psychological and philosophical theories of moral/character development, including Maslow, Erikson, Kohlberg, Gilligan, and McIntyre will be examined. Also, students will be assisted in developing practical strategies and methodologies for supporting character development in the context of Christian Education.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completing the course, students should be able to:
a. examine their self’s own understandings and philosophies of moral character formation in Christian education.
b. develop a critical understanding of theories and rationales underlying approaches of moral character education.
c. identify ways in implementation of moral character education in Churches and in Christian schools.
d. apply concepts in moral character education to specific ministry contexts.
e. critique theories of moral character education by participant observation and empirical research.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Methods and Paradigms of Christian Studies
courses.description: This course aims at providing students with a solid methodological and theoretical understanding of the multidisciplinary study of Christianity. It mainly introduces the students to the principal tasks (e.g., historical, constructive, practical) and methods, together with their theoretical presuppositions, of Christian studies. It also acquaints students with major theological paradigms (e.g., traditional, liberal, liberationist, feminist, etc.) and their different visions of the theological disciplines (e.g., biblical studies, history of Christianity, systematic theology, pastoral studies, etc.). Issues such as the relation of Christian studies to other academic fields, the alleged conflict between its scientific and ecclesial orientations, and the interconnection of its diverse disciplines, will be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Christian Studies and MA in Religious Studies programmes.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To obtain a broadened and deepened understanding of the major traditions of Christianity in the world in historical and comparative perspectives
2. To be able to understand major theological paradigms in Christianity with their internal complexity, and be able to extend such understanding to issues in church and society
3. To have some knowledge of the tasks and methods of the major disciplines in Christian studies and be able to apply such knowledge in research

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: New Testament in Contexts
courses.description: This course will select some texts of the New Testament with contemporary methods for in-depth study. Texts include selected themes of the Pauline Epistles, Synoptic Gospels and Johannine Literature, e.g., Pauline Epistle Form, Doctrinal and Ethical Teachings; Eucharist, Baptism, Miracles and Teachings of the Synoptics; as well as Revelation structure, “I am saying”, Farewell Discourse of the Gospel of John.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
Exclusion=Not for students who have taken THEO5312 Introduction to the New Testament
For students in MA Religious Studies or MA Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students should be able to:
Expected Knowledge Outcomes
1. Know how to find reliable and trustworthy resources for their own reconstruction of socio-historical contexts of the New Testament;
2. Compare and contrast New Testament studies in public domain with uncritical voices by means of established paradigms and academic consensus;
Expected Skills Outcome
3. Analyze context(s) behind primary texts and evaluate their relevance in biblical exegeses; (\* This also serve as a preparation of key research skills for graduate work in advanced biblical studies)
Expected Attitude Outcome
4. Deepen their critical and yet sympathetic understanding of earliest Christian traditions in our contemporary contexts and appraise their contributions in shaping different cultures.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Contextual Interpretation of the Bible
courses.description: This course introduces some methodologies to read the Bible texts, where the perspectives of readers take primary focus. Defined by their specific contexts such as social, political, historical, philosophical and theological ones, it instructs how one can interpret the Bible meaningfully for their communities of faith. Some of these include postcolonial and post-imperialist interpretations, ethnic interpretations, and interpretations for the disabled, etc. Emphases are given to how these methodologies come about and has developed in the academic disciplines, the components of these methodologies and how they may be applied to the reading of the Bible.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Describe and explain the historical, political, social, cultural and economic contexts of particular communities.
2. Review and analyse the scholarship of the biblical text/s and theology, and explain how traditional interpretations of the Bible in Christian history marginalize and oppress these communities.
3. Delineate the history of oppression of these communities by Christian theology and interpretations.
4. Review and evaluate how recent scholarship in Contextual Interpretations of the Bible contributes to specific communities. Point out the specific contributions as well as criticize the limitations. Make judgments on the relevance and significance of such interpretations, taking seriously as well the contexts of the biblical books.
5. Construct and propose a re-interpretation of a bible passage/book for a specific marginalized community, taking into their contexts as primary focus and finding points of relevance in the biblical passage/book.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Biblical Theology
courses.description: Exegetical study of Old Testament and New Testament passages and their implication for contemporary church and society.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Review and list the major biblical theologians of the 20th century and their contributions.
2. Analyse and evaluate with specific historical events the reliability and relevance of their biblical theological formulations.
3. Comment and draw implications how some of the significant theologians effect the academia of Biblical Studies as well as churches/denominations of their time.
4. Critically review some of the controversial dogmas in relation to biblical theology. Point out and substantiate the exegetical fallacies and propose what it should be.
5. Distinguish ‘cultural memory’ in biblical studies and draw relevance to biblical theology.
6. Design and propose an outline of a biblical theology that factor in biblical criticisms as well as make it relevant to specific faith communities of today.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Methods and Biblical Interpretation
courses.description: Biblical interpretation does not happen in a vacuum. Every interpretive act involves the text, the reader, and its signifying context, including that of the writer(s) and that of the reader, defined by the complex web of social, cultural, political, and even psychological forces. This course covers some major methods used in the critical study of the Bible (with a focus on the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament) from the late nineteenth century to the early twenty-first century, including the historical-critical methods, literary criticism, and reader-centered approaches. It examines the tasks, presuppositions, and reading strategies of various exegetical methods, and evaluates each’s weaknesses and strengths.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Christian Studies, Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students should be able to:
• Describe and compare various critical methods of biblical studies
• Deepen their awareness of how the writer’s and interpreter’s social, cultural, political, and even psychological contexts may affect the process of signification
• Demonstrate a familiarity of the current approaches to biblical interpretation
• Be able to apply at least seven of the critical methods in their reading of the biblical texts
• Be able to formulate their own intersectional and interdisciplinary approach to biblical interpretation

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: The Hebrew Bible in Contexts
courses.description: "This course aims at introducing students to the approaches to reading the Hebrew Bible (The Christian Old Testament) in its literary, socio-political and religio-cultural contexts. The literary setting and historical background will be surveyed and explored in order to enhance students’ understanding of the text and the dynamics of the reading process."

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Contextual Theologies
courses.description: This course tries to critically examine several features of all theological endeavours: particularity, contextuality and historicity. It also articulates how theologies are spatially and temporally shaped. Accordingly, the relationship between theology and context will not be conceived as a kind of linear application of some ready-made theologies to the contemporary contexts, but a kind of interpretive effort which tries to correlate the Christian traditions with the contemporary cultural, socio-political and economical context. It will also discuss the practical dimension of the ‘doing’ of theologies. It is according to all this that some examples of contextual theology will be introduced.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Modern Christian Thinkers
courses.description: The course introduces the work and thought of some of the important theologians of the 20th century. Western thought since the period of the Enlightenment has understood human beings as autonomous from God. Modern science and human rationality left no place for God. The course attempts to understand how Christian faith and theology reacts to this challenge of modernity by presenting and studying different theological responses to it. The course puts emphasis on the reading of primary sources of various theologians.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Christian Studies and Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
• The students will be able to critically engage with difficult texts of modern Christian thinkers.
• The students will learn to critically evaluate the soundness of different approaches to modern society and make appropriate judgment about multiple theological perspectives.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Asian Theologies
courses.description: Asia is a large continent with the largest population in the world and a diverse cultural heritage. Though Christianity was born in West Asia, its expansion to South and East Asia happened rather recently. In the last few decades, Asians have begun to utilize their own resources and context in theological endeavour. This course attempts to investigate some of the theologies emerging in Asia.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Christianity in Chinese Religious Context
courses.description: This course aims at studying Chinese Christianity in the Chinese religious context. Special emphasis will be given to the question as to how Christianity has been viewed in and shaped by the Chinese religious context. Comparison between some of the Chinese Christian phenomena and their counterparts in the traditional Chinese religions will be made, e.g., the Taiping Christianity vis-à-vis the Buddhist or Taoist Messianic movements. Issues on Christianity faces in the Chinese religious context will also be discussed, e.g., syncretism and dual religious citizenship.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Christianity and Social Change
courses.description: In the absence of any social theory that is uniquely “Christian”, this course will seek to study the positions of the Christian churches on various political and social issues as they seek to define for themselves their role in a rapidly changing world. Asian models and the more traditional Western approaches to similar issues will be compared in order to highlight the strength and weaknesses of each in the common attempt to balance the Christian ideal and social realities.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes: After completing this course, the student will (i) obtain a basic understanding of the major characteristics of modern society in several dimensions, the processes of social change leading to such characteristics, and the impact on Christianity; (ii) understand how Christian churches, organizations, and individuals in several social, cultural, and historical situations have responded to social changes in modernity; (iii) be acquainted with the critical analysis of modernity by a few social theorists; (iv) critically analyze the relation between Christianity and social change about a case, event, or issue in modernity, and constructively articulate a response.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Chinese Christianities
courses.description: This course examines various issues regarding the course of Christianity indigenization and contextualization in China, such as the development of Nestorian Christianity in Tang Dynasty, Jesuits mission and the Rites Controversy, the issue of Chinese Bible translation and Christian literature, Christianity and social reform and reconstruction in China, independent churches and evangelists in China, and the issue of Christianity and races. By discussing the above issues, this course shall explore how the Chinese experience would contribute to the enrichment of church universal.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students are expected to, by the end of the course,
1. Show their concrete knowledge of certain terms and concepts, such as indigenization, contextualisation, localisation, inculturation and interculturation.
2. Be able to critically reflect on issues regarding Christianity indigenization in China from historical perspectives.
3. Demonstrate their abilities to reflect on and evaluate, from theological perspectives, the efforts towards Christianity indigenization by Chinese Christians.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Christianity and Chinese Culture
courses.description: Starting from the traditional understanding of indigenization whereby culture are often looked upon as static entities, Christianity and Chinese culture will also be compared as they moved through the recent history of China as two living forces competing to shape the China that was to be. This is an open-ended course which will continuously be informed by recent trends and developments.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Religious Studies or Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Christianity in Twentieth Century China
courses.description: This course examines the development of Christian thoughts and institutions in China from the early twentieth century to the present.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students are expected to
1. Recognize the basic knowledge of several important issues regarding the development of Christianity in twentieth century China.
2. Demonstrate their understanding of the interactive relationships between Christianity and socio-political context in modern and contemporary China.
3. Show a deeper understanding of the historical causes behind the status quo of Christianity in China.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: History of Christian Thought
courses.description: This course consists of a critical survey of the history of the development of Christian (mainly theological) thought. It will concentrate on analysis of several decisive phrases of development and will attempt to show the interaction between Christian thought and its historical circumstances.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes: After completing this course, the student is expected (a) to have a solid overview of the development of Christian thought, including the diversity of views, major historical developments, and significant issues involved, and their interrelations; (b) to be able to understand and appreciate some important theologians, including their life and thought; (c) to be able to critically articulate the relevance of Christian thoughts in personal life, churches, and society.

meetings.instructor:

Ms. PANG Wai Yu

courses.description: This course helps students perceive doing theology as taking place within the ethical debates of society as a whole. It introduces different ways of how theology has entered or can entered, both historically and methodologically, into debate on shared ground with social sciences, politics and economics, etc. Different theological perspectives, such as those put forward by Reinhold Niebuhr, Max Stackhouse, and Duncan Forrester on the one hand, and Howard Yoder, Stanley Hauerwas, John Milbank and others, on the other hand, will be discussed. Students will also be shown how these perspectives can be applied to the discussion of local public issues.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To review critically different theological opinions on public theologies.
2. To be engaged into a fruitful dialogue between theology and other disciplines, such as, politics and economics on public life.
3. To correlate the knowledge developed in the course to the Christian practice in Hong Kong, and to evaluate it critically .
4. To use public reasoning to communicate the findings to a range of audiences.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Theology and Work
courses.description: Work can be a creative expression of the way one professes commitment, service and personal gift to a community. This course is to provide a Christian critique of the contemporary practice of work and retrieve the dignity of work. Concepts related to work like vocation, leisure, play and Sabbath would be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To evaluate theologically the ideologies and practice of work.
2. To extend the knowledge and skill developed in the course for reflecting a work ethics that upholds human dignity.
3. To use public reasoning to communicate the findings to a range of audiences

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Media, Popular Culture and Christianity
courses.description: This course is a critical exploration of the intricate relationships between popular media culture and Christianity. While popular culture and the media have long become a daily reality for many in the world, these have seldom been taken seriously by theologians and scholars of religion. Also, the relationship between popular media and religion (including Christianity) is often overlooked in academic studies until relatively recent time. We shall re-examine various manifestations of popular culture from Christian theological perspectives, and also probes into the subtle interrelatedness between media culture and Christianity as an organised religion. As its wider academic context, this course engages with the interdisciplinary field of media, religion, and culture (MRC) which has been under vigorous development since the mid-1990s; as its immediate socio-cultural-religious context of discussions, it attends particularly to the Chinese language popular media and Chinese Christianity in Hong Kong.

2. Students learn the critical skills to theologize counseling theories with a mutually critical correlational perspective.
3. Students start to appreciate the possibilities of integration between social scientific theories and theological traditions.

courses.description: This course examines topics and issues related to Christianity in China, such as the approaches and strategies of Christian missions, the development of missionary enterprises, church-state relationships, church-mission relationships, the adaptation of the Christian faith to Chinese culture, Christianity and social reconstruction in China, independent Christian movement, etc. Students are allowed to take these courses for more than once.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity or MA Christian Studies or MA Theological Studies
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate their knowledge of the selected topics and issues related to the evolution of Christianity in China. Additionally, they shall be able to develop the ability to critically reflect and evaluate, from various angles, on those topics and issues. Furthermore, students are also expected to show their abilities to carry out independent research on the topics in accordance of the course selected issues.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Theology and Hong Kong Society

meetings.instructor:
Mrs MA LUK Siu Ling, 
Professor KUNG Lap Yan

courses.description: This course equips students with knowledge and skills in theologizing with an interdisciplinary horizon across a variety of aspects of everyday practical life in Hong Kong. It helps students to see how different sub-disciplines of theology can be critically integrated into a coordinated whole and in this way be relevant to the practical life in one's own context. Social and theological analysis are given equal emphasis, and how these two could be mutually and critically correlated will be demonstrated. Experts or/and experienced practitioners in different fields of practice will be invited to share with students their analyses of the respective public/current issues, while theological responses (philosophical, exegetical, historical, and practical) will be given by teachers from different sub-disciplines in theology. Around half of the lectures will be structured in the form of an interdisciplinary dialogue.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite = THEO5906 Methods and Paradigms of Christian Studies or THEO5336 Systematic Theology II
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the completion of this course, students should be able to achieve the below:

Knowledge Aspect

1. Acquire a general but critical framework to integrate various sub-disciplines of theology for a practical analysis and evaluation of the Hong Kong society.

2. Demonstrate a contextual understanding of a variety of models of publicization of theology.

Skill Aspect

1. Acquire the ability to apply an interdisciplinary approach to a theological analysis and evaluation of the Hong Kong society in some selected aspects (please refer to Course Syllabus).

2. Begin to be able to formulate one's own initial interdisciplinary framework to do contextual theological analyses of one's own place.

Values and Attitudes Aspect

1. Appreciate the importance of an interdisciplinary horizon to any theological understanding of one's own society.

2. Critically aware of the role of theology in public sphere of one's own place.

3. Appreciate the value of defragmentation of theological study.

courses.subject: THEO
courses.title: Clinical Pastoral Education
courses.description: Clinical Pastoral Education (CPE) is a mode of theological education that has a history of several decades. It facilitates pastoral growth through action-reflection mode of learning in clinical settings. This course requires students to complete one unit of CPE programme at a training center recognized by the Divinity School.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Divinity
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students begin to articulate the central themes of their religious heritage and the theological understanding that informs their ministry.

2. Students are equipped to identify and discuss major life events, relationships and cultural contexts that influence personal identity as expressed in pastoral functioning.

3. Students are able to initiate peer group and supervisory consultation and receive critique about one’s practice.

4. Students begin to acquire the basic skills to recognize relational dynamics within group contexts.

5. Students being to demonstrate integration of conceptual understandings presented in the curriculum into pastoral practice.

6. Students are equipped with basic skills and knowledge to initiate helping relationships within and across diverse populations.

7. Students begin to use the clinical methods of learning to achieve their educational goals.

8. Students are able to formulate clear and specific goals for continuing pastoral formation with reference to personal strengths and weaknesses.
